title: Continuous opioid antagonist supply in high opiate overdose areas, including over-the-counter antagonists, and notice of insufficient stock
rule_summary: M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 19C provides that the board of registration in pharmacy shall promulgate regulations requiring pharmacies located in areas with high incidence of opiate overdose, as determined by the board in consultation with the department, to maintain a continuous supply of opioid antagonists, as defined in s. 19B; provided that the continuous supply of opioid antagonists shall include opioid antagonists that are approved by the United States Food and Drug Administration to be sold over the counter without a prescription; and provided further that such pharmacies shall notify the department if the supply or stock of opioid antagonist doses is insufficient to enable compliance with maintaining a continuous supply of opioid antagonists.
exam_relevance: Tests which pharmacies the continuous-supply requirement reaches, who determines the high-incidence areas, that the continuous supply includes opioid antagonists approved to be sold over the counter without a prescription, and that such a pharmacy notifies the department when its supply or stock is insufficient to maintain a continuous supply.
common_confusions: Treating over-the-counter opioid antagonists as outside the continuous supply the section describes.
Overlooking the notice to the department when the supply or stock of opioid antagonist doses is insufficient to maintain a continuous supply.
Applying the continuous-supply requirement to pharmacies outside areas with high incidence of opiate overdose.
verification_notes: Read in the current text of M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 19C on malegislature.gov on 2026-09-14.
